chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Abu Suleyman al-Hazza' al-Jabali, from Muhammad ibn al-Fayz, who said:

I had lunch with Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), and upon the food-spread were vegetables, and with us was an old man who avoided the endive. So Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: 'But you all are thinking that the endive is cold, and it is not like that, but it is moderate, and its merits upon the vegetables is like our merits upon the people'.

key_terms.الْهِنْدَبَاءَ: Endive, a type of leafy vegetable

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the nature of endive and what analogy does the Imam use regarding the Imams?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) corrects the prevailing folk belief that endive is 'cold' by defining it as 'moderate' (*mu'tadal*), thereby refining the medical understanding of the time. He employs a profound analogy, comparing the superior quality of endive among vegetables to the spiritual and authoritative superiority of the Ahl al-Bayt among all of humanity, highlighting their unique status in Shia theology.
